body.en:
The Bootstrap grid system is a mobile-first, flexbox-based layout system that divides the page width into 12 equal columns. Using rows and columns, content can be arranged in any layout, and the layout changes automatically at different screen sizes (breakpoints).

Three main parts

  1. Container (.container or .container-fluid): centres and pads the content. Every grid must be inside a container.
  2. Row (.row): a horizontal group of columns. It is a flex container with negative margins that line up columns with the container edge.
  3. Column (.col-*): holds the content. The number tells how many of the 12 columns it spans.
<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-sm-4">Column 1</div>
    <div class="col-sm-8">Column 2</div>
  </div>
</div>

Rules of the grid

  • Rows must be placed inside a container; only columns can be direct children of rows.
  • Content goes inside columns, not directly in rows.
  • The total of the column numbers in one row should be 12. If it is more than 12, the extra columns wrap onto a new line.
  • Columns have horizontal padding called the gutter; it can be changed with g-*, gx-*, gy-*.
  • Column classes apply to their breakpoint and all larger screens.
<div class="row g-0">no gutter</div>
<div class="row g-4">large gutter</div>
<div class="row gx-5 gy-2">x and y separately</div>

A column class has the form .col-{breakpoint}-{number}.

xs
<576		sm
>=576		md
>=768		lg
>=992		xl
>=1200		xxl
>=1400
Class prefix.col-.col-sm-.col-md-.col-lg-.col-xl-.col-xxl-
Container width100%540px720px960px1140px1320px

Types of column classes

  • .col: equal-width columns that share the row automatically.
  • .col-{n}: n of 12 columns on all screen sizes (e.g. .col-6 = half).
  • .col-{bp}-{n}: n columns from that breakpoint upward; below it the column is full width (stacked).
  • .col-auto: width according to the content.
  • Mixing classes: col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3 gives 1, 2 or 4 columns per row.
  • .row-cols-{n} on the row sets how many columns appear per row.
<!-- equal width -->
<div class="row">
  <div class="col">1</div>
  <div class="col">2</div>
</div>
<!-- mobile: stacked, tablet: 2, desktop: 4 -->
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">A</div>
  <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">B</div>
  <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">C</div>
  <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-3">D</div>
</div>
<!-- width from content, rest auto -->
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-auto">Label</div>
  <div class="col">Rest</div>
</div>
<!-- columns per row set on the row -->
<div class="row row-cols-2 row-cols-lg-4 g-3">...</div>

Example: for a page with 3 boxes in a row on desktop but stacked on mobile, use col-md-4 on each box.

A container is the outermost layout element. It holds rows and columns, centres the content and adds padding at the left and right.

ContainerBehaviour
.containerResponsive fixed width: max-width changes at each breakpoint (540, 720, 960, 1140, 1320 px); 100% below 576 px
.container-fluidAlways 100% of the screen width
.container-{sm|md|lg|xl|xxl}100% wide until that breakpoint, then fixed like .container
<div class="container">fixed width per breakpoint</div>
<div class="container-fluid">always 100% wide</div>
<div class="container-md">100% until md, then fixed</div>
  • Use .container for normal page content, so lines do not become too long on big screens.
  • Use .container-fluid for full-width headers, footers, banners and dashboards.
  • Containers can be nested, but usually this is not required.

Offset classes move a column to the right by leaving empty columns on its left. They increase the left margin of the column by a number of grid columns.

  • Syntax: .offset-{n} or responsive .offset-{bp}-{n} (n = 1 to 11).
  • .col-md-4 .offset-md-4: the column starts after 4 empty columns.
  • .col-md-6 .offset-md-3: centres a half-width column (3 + 6 + 3 = 12).
  • Reset an offset at a larger breakpoint with .offset-lg-0.
  • Margin utilities can also separate columns: .ms-auto pushes a column to the right, .me-auto to the left.
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-md-4">.col-md-4</div>
  <div class="col-md-4 offset-md-4">
    .col-md-4 .offset-md-4</div>
</div>
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-md-6 offset-md-3">centred</div>
</div>
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-4">left</div>
  <div class="col-4 ms-auto">pushed right</div>
</div>

Bootstrap 3: .col-md-offset-4. Bootstrap 4/5: .offset-md-4.

Reordering changes the visual order of columns without changing the order in the HTML code. It uses the flexbox order property.

  • .order-0 to .order-5: set the order value; smaller values appear first. Columns without an order class have order 0.
  • .order-first (order: -1) and .order-last (order: 6).
  • Responsive: .order-{bp}-{value}, e.g. .order-md-2 works from 768 px.
<div class="row">
  <div class="col order-3">First in HTML</div>
  <div class="col order-1">Second in HTML</div>
  <div class="col order-2">Third in HTML</div>
</div>
<!-- different order on phone and desktop -->
<div class="row">
  <main class="col-md-8 order-md-2">Main</main>
  <aside class="col-md-4 order-md-1">Sidebar</aside>
</div>

Why reorder?

  • On a phone, the main content should come first, but on a desktop a sidebar on the left looks better.
  • Search engines and screen readers read the HTML order, so important content can be written first in HTML.

Bootstrap 3 used .col-md-push-* and .col-md-pull-*; they were replaced by order classes in Bootstrap 4.

Nesting means placing a new .row with its own columns inside an existing column. It is used to make complex layouts.

  • The nested row must be placed inside a column.
  • The nested row again has 12 columns, which divide the width of the parent column (not the whole page).
  • Nested columns can use any column classes, offsets and order classes.
  • Nesting can be repeated at any depth.
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-sm-9">
    Level 1: .col-sm-9
    <div class="row">
      <div class="col-6">Level 2: .col-6</div>
      <div class="col-6">Level 2: .col-6</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-3">Level 1: .col-sm-3</div>
</div>

Example: a col-md-8 news area containing two col-sm-6 news boxes. Each inner box is half of the news area, i.e. 4 of the 12 page columns.

1. Responsive: one layout works on all screen sizes; columns stack, resize or rearrange automatically.
  2. Mobile first: designed for small screens and enhanced for large screens.
  3. Simple to use: only classes are needed; no media queries or float calculations.
  4. Flexible 12-column system: 12 can be divided into 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12 equal parts.
  5. Six breakpoints (xs to xxl) for fine control.
  6. Flexbox based: equal-height columns, vertical alignment (align-items-center), horizontal alignment (justify-content-between) and auto-width columns.
  7. Offset, reorder and nesting allow complex layouts.
  8. Gutters give consistent spacing that can be changed easily.
  9. Consistent and cross-browser: the same layout in all modern browsers; a team uses the same system.
  10. Saves development time and keeps the HTML organised.

Practical 5 (class time table) shows how the grid turns a table-like design into a layout that rearranges itself on phones.

title.en: 2.2 Responsive Images, Image Shapes, Typography and Tables

body.en:
Responsive images

The class .img-fluid makes an image responsive. It applies max-width: 100%; and height: auto; so the image scales down with its parent element but never becomes larger than its real size. (Bootstrap 3: .img-responsive.)

<img src="images/campus.jpg" class="img-fluid"
  alt="Campus">
<img src="a.jpg" class="rounded" alt="...">
<img src="b.jpg" class="rounded-circle" alt="...">
<img src="c.jpg" class="img-thumbnail" alt="...">
<img src="d.jpg" class="rounded mx-auto d-block"
  alt="centred">
<img src="e.jpg" class="float-end" alt="right">

Image shapes / styles

ClassEffect
.roundedRounded corners (sizes .rounded-0 to .rounded-5)
.rounded-circleCircle (ellipse if the image is not square)
.rounded-pillCapsule shape
.img-thumbnail1 px border, padding and rounded corners
.rounded-top / -end / -bottom / -startRound only one side

Aligning images

  • .float-start / .float-end: float left or right (text wraps around).
  • .mx-auto .d-block: centre a block image; or .text-center on the parent for an inline image.

Figures

<figure class="figure">
  <img src="lab.jpg" class="figure-img img-fluid rounded"
    alt="Lab">
  <figcaption class="figure-caption text-center">
    Computer lab</figcaption>
</figure>

Always use the alt attribute to describe the image. The <picture> element with srcset can load different image files for different screen sizes.

Typography means the style and appearance of text. Bootstrap sets a default font size of 1rem (16 px), line height 1.5 and a native system font stack, and provides classes for headings, paragraphs, inline text, lists and alignment.

Headings and display headings

<h1>h1 heading</h1>   <p class="h1">p styled as h1</p>
<h3>Main title
  <small class="text-body-secondary">sub title</small>
</h3>
<h1 class="display-1">Display 1</h1>
<p class="lead">Lead paragraph stands out.</p>
  • <h1> to <h6> and the classes .h1 to .h6 (heading look on any element).
  • .display-1 to .display-6: larger, lighter headings for hero sections.
  • <small> inside a heading, with .text-body-secondary, gives a secondary title.
  • .lead: larger paragraph for an introduction.

Inline text elements

<mark>highlight</mark>  <del>deleted</del>
<s>no longer true</s>   <ins>inserted</ins>
<u>underline</u>        <small>fine print</small>
<strong>bold</strong>   <em>italic</em>
<abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>

Blockquotes

<blockquote class="blockquote">
  <p>Write less, do more.</p>
</blockquote>
<figcaption class="blockquote-footer">
  jQuery <cite title="Motto">motto</cite>
</figcaption>

Lists

<ul class="list-unstyled"> ... </ul>
<ul class="list-inline">
  <li class="list-inline-item">HTML</li>
  <li class="list-inline-item">CSS</li>
</ul>

Text utility classes

<p class="text-start">left</p>
<p class="text-center">centre</p>
<p class="text-end">right</p>
<p class="text-md-center">centre from md</p>
<p class="text-uppercase">upper</p>
<p class="text-capitalize">each word capital</p>
<p class="fw-bold">bold</p> <p class="fst-italic">italic</p>
<p class="text-primary">blue</p> <p class="text-muted">grey</p>
<p class="text-truncate">very long text ...</p>
  • Alignment: text-start, text-center, text-end (responsive: text-md-start).
  • Transform: text-lowercase, text-uppercase, text-capitalize.
  • Weight and style: fw-bold, fw-semibold, fw-normal, fw-light, fst-italic.
  • Size: fs-1 to fs-6. Wrapping: text-wrap, text-nowrap, text-truncate.
  • Decoration: text-decoration-underline, text-decoration-line-through, text-decoration-none.

Add the base class .table to any <table> to get Bootstrap styling (padding, horizontal dividers, full width). Other classes add more styles.

ClassEffect
.tableBasic styling (required)
.table-stripedZebra stripes on rows
.table-striped-columnsStripes on columns
.table-borderedBorders on all sides of every cell
.table-borderlessNo borders
.table-hoverHighlight row on mouse over
.table-smCompact: cell padding halved
.table-dark / .table-lightDark or light table or header
.table-activeHighlight a row or cell
.table-primary, -success, -danger, -warning, -info, -secondaryContextual colours on a table, row or cell
.table-responsiveOn a wrapper div: horizontal scroll on small screens
.caption-topShow the <caption> above the table
<table class="table table-striped table-hover">
  <thead class="table-dark">
    <tr><th>Roll</th><th>Name</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>1</td><td>Aman</td></tr>
    <tr class="table-success"><td>2</td><td>Bhumi</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Responsive tables

Wide tables cannot shrink below their content width. Wrapping them in .table-responsive (or .table-responsive-sm/md/lg/xl/xxl) adds horizontal scrolling inside the box instead of breaking the page layout.

<div class="table-responsive">
  <table class="table table-bordered"> ... </table>
</div>

Bootstrap 3: row classes .success, .danger, .active, .table-condensed. Bootstrap 5: .table-success, .table-danger, .table-active, .table-sm.

Bootstrap styles forms consistently in all browsers and offers several layouts.

1. Vertical form (default)

Labels appear above full-width controls. Each group gets a margin class (.mb-3).

<form>
  <div class="mb-3">
    <label for="email" class="form-label">Email</label>
    <input type="email" class="form-control" id="email">
    <div class="form-text">Help text</div>
  </div>
  <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Submit</button>
</form>

2. Grid form

Use .row and .col-* to place several fields in one row (e.g. first and last name side by side).

3. Horizontal form

Labels and controls are side by side. Each field is a .row; the label gets a column class plus .col-form-label (vertically centred with the input).

<div class="row mb-3">
  <label for="city" class="col-sm-2 col-form-label">City</label>
  <div class="col-sm-10">
    <input type="text" class="form-control" id="city">
  </div>
</div>

4. Inline form

All fields in one line on larger screens, using .row-cols-lg-auto and .align-items-center; they stack on phones.

<form class="row row-cols-lg-auto g-3 align-items-center">
  <div class="col-12">
    <input class="form-control" placeholder="Username">
  </div>
  <div class="col-12">
    <button class="btn btn-primary">Login</button>
  </div>
</form>

Important form classes

  • .form-label for labels; .form-text for help text.
  • .form-control for text inputs and textareas; .form-select for select boxes.
  • .col-form-label in horizontal forms.
  • Bootstrap 3's .form-group, .form-horizontal and .form-inline were replaced by grid and spacing utilities.

Form controls

<input class="form-control form-control-lg">
<select class="form-select"><option>One</option></select>
<textarea class="form-control" rows="3"></textarea>

<div class="form-check">
  <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" id="c1">
  <label class="form-check-label" for="c1">Check</label>
</div>
<div class="form-check form-switch">
  <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" id="s1">
  <label class="form-check-label" for="s1">Switch</label>
</div>
<input type="range" class="form-range">

<div class="form-floating">
  <input class="form-control" id="n" placeholder="Name">
  <label for="n">Name</label>
</div>
  • Text inputs (.form-control): sizes .form-control-lg, .form-control-sm; attributes readonly, disabled; .form-control-plaintext for read-only plain text.
  • Select (.form-select): also sizes and multiple.
  • Checkboxes and radios: .form-check wrapper, .form-check-input, .form-check-label; .form-check-inline places them in a row.
  • Switches: add .form-switch to a checkbox's .form-check.
  • Range: .form-range. File input: .form-control with type="file". Colour: .form-control-color.
  • Floating labels: .form-floating; the input comes before the label and needs a placeholder.
  • Input groups: .input-group + .input-group-text for prefixes such as +91 or @.

Form validation

Bootstrap uses the browser's HTML5 validation (required, type="email", pattern, min, maxlength) and shows coloured feedback:

<form class="needs-validation" novalidate>
  <input class="form-control" required>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">Required.</div>
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Submit</button>
</form>
<script>
  form.addEventListener("submit", function (e) {
    if (!form.checkValidity()) e.preventDefault();
    form.classList.add("was-validated");
  });
</script>
  • novalidate on the form turns off the browser's default pop-up messages.
  • Adding .was-validated to the form shows red borders and .invalid-feedback text for invalid fields, green borders and .valid-feedback for valid ones.
  • For server-side validation, add .is-invalid or .is-valid to individual fields.

Buttons are created with the base class .btn plus a variant class. They can be used on <button>, <a> and <input> elements.

<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Primary</button>
<button class="btn btn-outline-success">Outline</button>
<button class="btn btn-danger btn-lg">Large</button>
<button class="btn btn-secondary btn-sm">Small</button>
<button class="btn btn-primary" disabled>Disabled</button>
<a href="#" class="btn btn-link" role="button">Link</a>
<input type="reset" class="btn btn-warning" value="Reset">

<div class="d-grid gap-2">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Block button</button>
</div>
TypeClasses
Coloursbtn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-success, btn-danger, btn-warning, btn-info, btn-light, btn-dark, btn-link
Outlinebtn-outline-primary, btn-outline-danger, ...
Sizesbtn-lg, btn-sm (Bootstrap 3 also had btn-xs)
Block (full width)wrapper .d-grid (BS4: btn-block)
States.active, disabled attribute (or .disabled on <a>)
Toggledata-bs-toggle="button"
Close button.btn-close
  • For an <a> used as a button, add role="button".
  • Always set type on <button> (submit, reset or button).
  • Button groups and toolbars are covered in Unit 3.

A caret is the small triangle (arrow) shown on a button or link to indicate that it opens a dropdown menu.

  • In Bootstrap 5, the class .dropdown-toggle adds the caret automatically using a CSS ::after pseudo-element.
  • In Bootstrap 3, the caret was a separate element: <span class="caret"></span>.
  • The caret direction follows the wrapper class: .dropdown (down), .dropup (up), .dropend (right), .dropstart (left).
  • .dropdown-toggle-split makes a split button with the caret on a separate part.
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn btn-primary dropdown-toggle"
    data-bs-toggle="dropdown">Menu</button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">One</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
<!-- .dropup  .dropend  .dropstart change the direction -->

Dropdowns need bootstrap.bundle.min.js (includes Popper) and the attribute data-bs-toggle="dropdown". They are studied in detail in Units 3 and 4.

h.en: Hide or Show Text in Bootstrap

body.en:
Bootstrap display utility classes show or hide elements, and they can depend on the screen size.

Format: .d-{value} for all sizes or .d-{breakpoint}-{value} from a breakpoint upward. Values: none, inline, inline-block, block, grid, table, flex, inline-flex.

<div class="d-none">always hidden</div>
<div class="d-none d-md-block">hidden on phones only</div>
<div class="d-block d-md-none">visible on phones only</div>
<div class="d-none d-lg-block d-xl-none">only on lg</div>
<span class="invisible">hidden, keeps space</span>
<span class="visually-hidden">for screen readers</span>
<div class="d-print-none">not printed</div>
RequirementClasses
Hidden on all screens.d-none
Hidden only on xs (phones).d-none .d-sm-block
Hidden only on md.d-md-none .d-lg-block
Visible only on xs.d-block .d-sm-none
Visible only on lg.d-none .d-lg-block .d-xl-none
Hidden when printing.d-print-none

Other ways to hide

  • .invisible: hides the element but it still takes up space (visibility: hidden). .visible shows it again.
  • .visually-hidden: hides it from the screen but screen readers still read it (Bootstrap 3/4: .sr-only).
  • JavaScript: toggle the d-none class, e.g. element.classList.toggle("d-none"), or use the collapse plug-in (Unit 4).

Bootstrap 3 used .hidden-xs, .hidden-sm, .visible-md-block etc. Bootstrap 4/5 replaced them with d-* classes.

title.en: Student information using container and container-fluid (Practical 3)

code.en:
.container-fluid: always 100% wide

.container: fixed width per breakpoint

NameRiya Patel
Enrolment No.246070307051
BranchComputer Engineering
Semester3
CollegeGP Surat
.container-md: 100% wide below 768 px, then fixed
Footer in .container-fluid

programs.out:
A full-width blue header strip, then a box with a blue border holding the student details table (name, enrolment number, branch, semester, college), a grey .container-md box and a full-width black footer.
On a phone (390 px) every block is full width. On a desktop (1100 px) the header and footer still stretch edge to edge, while the student box and the grey box are 960 px wide and centred with white space on both sides.

expl.en:
• .container is a responsive fixed-width box, centred with auto margins. Its max-width is 540, 720, 960, 1140 and 1320 px at sm, md, lg, xl and xxl; below 576 px it is 100%.
  • .container-fluid is always 100% wide, at every screen size; it suits headers, footers and full-width banners.
  • .container-{breakpoint} (e.g. .container-md) is 100% wide until that breakpoint and then behaves like .container.
  • Every container has horizontal padding (gutter) so content does not touch the screen edge.
  • Utilities used: bg-primary, text-white, py-3 (vertical padding), my-3 (vertical margin), border.

title.en: Grid basics: rows, columns, sizes and breakpoints

code.en:
1. Equal-width columns: .col

col

col

2. Fixed: col-3 + col-6 + col-3

3
6
3

3. Responsive: col-12 col-md-4

C

4. Auto width: col-auto + col

col-auto
col (rest)

5. row-cols-2 row-cols-md-4

programs.out:
Five lavender demo rows.
1. Three equal columns side by side. 2. Columns of widths 3, 6 and 3 (the middle one is twice as wide). 3. A, B and C stacked on a phone, but in one row of three from 768 px. 4. A narrow box that is only as wide as its text, with the rest of the row filled by the second box. 5. Two boxes per row on a phone, four per row from 768 px.

expl.en:
• The grid structure is always .container > .row > .col-*. Content goes inside the columns, and only columns may be direct children of a row.
  • Each row has 12 columns. col-3 + col-6 + col-3 = 12. If the total is more than 12, the extra columns wrap to a new line.
  • .col without a number makes equal-width columns that share the row automatically.
  • .col-md-4 means 4 of 12 columns from md (768 px) upward; below that, col-12 gives full width (mobile first).
  • .col-auto sizes a column to its content. row-cols-* sets the number of columns per row on the row itself.
  • g-2 sets the gutter (gap) between columns; gx-* horizontal and gy-* vertical only.

code.en:
Offset columns

col-4
col-4 offset-4
col-6 offset-3 (centred)
col-md-5 offset-md-2
col-3
ms-auto

programs.out:
Row 1: a box on the left and a box on the right, with an empty gap of 4 columns between them.
Row 2: one box of half width, centred (3 empty columns on each side).
Row 3: on a phone the box is full width; from 768 px it is 5 columns wide and starts after 2 empty columns.
Row 4: one box at the far left and one pushed to the far right.

expl.en:
• Offset moves a column to the right by adding empty columns before it (it adds margin-left).
  • .offset-4 leaves 4 empty columns; total = offset + width must be 12 or less.
  • .col-6 .offset-3 centres a half-width column: 3 + 6 + 3 = 12.
  • Responsive offsets such as .offset-md-2 work only from that breakpoint upward; use .offset-md-0 to reset at a larger size.
  • Margin utilities ms-auto (margin-start: auto) and me-auto push columns to the opposite side.
  • Bootstrap 3 used col-md-offset-2; Bootstrap 4/5 use offset-md-2.

code.en:
Reordering columns

HTML order: First, Second, Third

First
Second (order-md-last)
Third (order-first)

order-1, order-2, order-3

A
B
C

programs.out:
Group 1 on a phone shows the boxes stacked as Third, First, Second. On a desktop (768 px and wider) they appear in one row as First, Third, Second, even though the HTML order is First, Second, Third.
Group 2 always shows B, C, A, because of the order-1, order-2 and order-3 classes.

expl.en:
• Reordering changes the visual order of columns without changing the HTML order. It uses the CSS flexbox order property.
  • .order-0 to .order-5 set the order number; lower numbers come first. Columns without a class have order 0.
  • .order-first (order -1) puts a column first and .order-last (order 6) puts it last.
  • Responsive versions such as .order-md-last apply only from that breakpoint, so the order can be different on phone and desktop.
  • Typical use: on a phone show the main content first and the sidebar after it, but on a desktop show the sidebar on the left.
  • Bootstrap 3 used col-md-push-* / col-md-pull-* instead.

code.en:
Nesting columns

Level 1: col-md-8
Level 2: col-6
Level 2: col-6
col-4
col-4
col-4
Level 1: col-md-4

programs.out:
A big lavender box "Level 1: col-md-8" contains its own row of two white boxes (col-6 each) and then three smaller white boxes (col-4 each). Next to it (on a desktop) or below it (on a phone) is the box "Level 1: col-md-4".
The inner boxes always split the parent's width into 12 again.

expl.en:
• Nesting means placing a new .row inside an existing column, and then columns inside that row.
  • The nested row again has 12 columns, measured relative to the width of the parent column, not the whole page. So the inner col-6 is half of the col-md-8 column.
  • A nested row must be inside a column, never directly inside another row.
  • Nesting is used for complex layouts, e.g. a main area with a list of product cards inside it.
  • There is no limit on nesting depth, but too many levels make the HTML hard to read.

  • Display headings .display-1 to .display-6 are larger, lighter headings; .lead makes a paragraph stand out.

  • Inline form: .row-cols-sm-auto makes each column only as wide as its content, so all fields fit in one line; .align-items-center aligns them vertically.

q.en: What is the Bootstrap grid system?

a.en: A mobile-first, flexbox-based layout system that divides the page into 12 columns using containers, rows and columns.

q.en: How many columns does the Bootstrap grid have?

a.en: 12 columns per row.

q.en: What are the three parts of the grid?

a.en: Container, row and column.

q.en: What happens if the columns in a row add up to more than 12?

a.en: The extra column(s) wrap onto a new line.

q.en: What is the difference between .container and .container-fluid?

a.en: .container has a fixed max-width at each breakpoint and is centred; .container-fluid is always 100% wide.

q.en: What is .container-md?

a.en: A container that is 100% wide below the md breakpoint (768 px) and fixed width from md upward.

q.en: What does col-md-6 mean?

a.en: The column takes 6 of 12 columns (half width) on screens 768 px and wider; on smaller screens it is full width.

q.en: What does .col (without a number) do?

a.en: It creates equal-width columns that share the row automatically.

q.en: What is .col-auto?

a.en: A column whose width depends on its content.

q.en: What is a gutter?

a.en: The space (padding) between columns, controlled with g-*, gx-* and gy-* classes.

q.en: What is an offset?

a.en: Empty columns added to the left of a column to move it right, e.g. offset-md-3.

q.en: How can a column be centred using offset?

a.en: col-md-6 offset-md-3 (3 + 6 + 3 = 12).

q.en: What is column reordering?

a.en: Changing the visual order of columns without changing the HTML, using order-* classes.

q.en: Which CSS property is used by order classes?

a.en: The flexbox order property.

q.en: What replaced push and pull classes of Bootstrap 3?

a.en: The order-* classes (order-first, order-last, order-md-2 etc.).

q.en: What is nesting of columns?

a.en: Placing a new row with columns inside an existing column.

q.en: In nesting, the 12 columns are relative to what?

a.en: The width of the parent column.

q.en: List two advantages of the Bootstrap grid.

a.en: Automatic responsive layouts without media queries, and flexible column sizes with offset, ordering and nesting.

q.en: Which class makes an image responsive?

a.en: .img-fluid (max-width: 100%; height: auto). Bootstrap 3 used .img-responsive.

q.en: How do you make a circular image?

a.en: Add .rounded-circle to a square image.

q.en: What does .img-thumbnail do?

a.en: Adds a 1 px border, padding and rounded corners like a thumbnail.

q.en: How can an image be centred?

a.en: Use .d-block .mx-auto on the image, or .text-center on its parent.

q.en: What is the default font size in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: 1rem, normally 16 px.

q.en: What are display headings?

a.en: Large, lighter headings with classes .display-1 to .display-6.

q.en: What does the .lead class do?

a.en: Makes a paragraph larger so it stands out.

q.en: Which tag highlights text?

a.en: The mark element.

q.en: What is the use of .list-unstyled?

a.en: It removes bullets and left padding from a list.

q.en: Which classes align text?

a.en: text-start, text-center and text-end (also responsive like text-md-center).

q.en: Which class is needed on every Bootstrap table?

a.en: .table

q.en: How do you create a striped table?

a.en: Add .table-striped to the table.

q.en: What does .table-hover do?

a.en: Highlights a table row when the mouse is over it.

q.en: How do you make a table responsive?

a.en: Wrap it in a div with class .table-responsive so it scrolls horizontally on small screens.

q.en: Name some contextual table classes.

a.en: table-primary, table-success, table-danger, table-warning, table-info, table-active.

q.en: Name the form layouts in Bootstrap.

a.en: Vertical (default), grid, horizontal and inline.

q.en: Which class styles text inputs?

a.en: .form-control

q.en: Which class styles a select box in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: .form-select

q.en: How is a horizontal form created?

a.en: Each field is a .row; the label uses a column class with .col-form-label and the input is placed in another column.

q.en: What are floating labels?

a.en: Labels shown inside the input that move up when the user types; created with .form-floating.

q.en: How do you create a switch?

a.en: Add .form-switch to the .form-check of a checkbox.

q.en: What is the use of novalidate?

a.en: It disables the browser's default validation pop-ups so Bootstrap's styled messages can be shown.

q.en: What does .was-validated do?

a.en: Shows valid (green) or invalid (red) styles and feedback messages for all fields in the form.

q.en: What is the base class of a Bootstrap button?

a.en: .btn

q.en: How do you create an outline button?

a.en: Use btn-outline-* classes, e.g. btn-outline-primary.

q.en: How is a full-width (block) button made in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: Place it in a wrapper with .d-grid (Bootstrap 4 used .btn-block).

q.en: What is a caret?

a.en: A small triangle that shows a button or link opens a dropdown menu.

q.en: How is a caret added in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: The .dropdown-toggle class adds it automatically (Bootstrap 3 used span.caret).

q.en: How do you hide an element on phones only?

a.en: Use .d-none .d-md-block (or .d-sm-block).

q.en: Difference between .d-none and .invisible?

a.en: .d-none removes the element from the layout; .invisible hides it but keeps its space.

q.en: What is .visually-hidden?

a.en: Hides content visually but keeps it for screen readers (Bootstrap 3/4: .sr-only).
